newsitem.title: LATVIA: COMPROMISE IN PRIVATISATION POSTS ROW - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: COMPROMISE IN PRIVATISATION POSTS ROW - REPORT.

text.p: The economy minister said, early on Thursday, that a compromise was reached in the row over the Privatisation Agency (LPA) board's membership and that two of the four board members will be replaced.
"There will be a competition held for two posts," economy minister Guntar Krasts told in an interview to Radio Latvia.
The government is expected to take a decision on the issue on Friday.

A row broke out last week when the economy minister demanded a full rotation in the LPA's board as their period in office comes to an end in April and criticised the agency for weak performance in privatising large state enterprises.
LPA head Janis Naglis, already reappointed to the post for the second term, had earlier said that he wanted to keep his team intact.

"I agreed with Janis Naglis that two persons should be replaced, Tiknuss and Freibergs," Krasts added. "The performance of these two people has not been so brilliant in the team and I accept that a competition might reveal new people."
Arvis Tiknuss is in-charge of the technical process of privatisation and Andrejs Freibers is the head of finances.
"Naglis agrees, and we all feel, that the pace of privatiasation is not sufficient," Krasts said in the interview to Radio Latvia.
"Most important in this compromise is that LPA will be able to carry on with its work after April 22-23 and both sides have made equal concessions," Janis Naglis said in the interview.
